pr.title: feat(upsampling) - Support upsampled error count with performance optimizations

raw_findings.body: A mode-160000 gitlink with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry is added, producing a broken/unresolvable submodule reference that fails submodule initialization and confuses tooling; it is unrelated to the upsampling feature.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Repository consumers that resolve submodules fail because the referenced commit/URL cannot be resolved.
raw_findings.impact: A mode-160000 gitlink with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry is added, producing a broken/unresolvable submodule reference that fails submodule initialization and confuses tooling; it is unrelated to the upsampling feature.
raw_findings.root_cause: A nested checkout of the repository was accidentally staged as a submodule pointer.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the `sentry-repo` gitlink from the commit (`git rm --cached sentry-repo`) before merge.
raw_findings.title: Accidental gitlink `sentry-repo` submodule committed at repository root
raw_findings.trigger: Any clone/checkout with `git clone --recurse-submodules`, CI checkout actions with submodule support, or `git submodule update` after this merge.

raw_findings.body: The eligibility check evaluates the wrong dataset, so widget-split error subqueries against discover/errors never get the upsampled count transformation (or vice versa), producing counts inconsistent with the non-split path for allowlisted projects.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Error counts from dashboard split queries are not upsampled while direct queries are, yielding divergent numbers for the same data.
raw_findings.impact: The eligibility check evaluates the wrong dataset, so widget-split error subqueries against discover/errors never get the upsampled count transformation (or vice versa), producing counts inconsistent with the non-split path for allowlisted projects.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new eligibility call inside `_get_event_stats` references the enclosing scope's `dataset` variable rather than the function's `scoped_dataset` argument, which the dashboard-split caller deliberately overrides.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass `scoped_dataset` (the actual dataset being queried by this invocation) into `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` instead of the closed-over `dataset`.
raw_findings.title: Upsampling eligibility uses closed-over `dataset` instead of the `scoped_dataset` parameter
raw_findings.trigger: Dashboard-widget dataset-split flow in `get_event_stats_factory` (dashboardWidgetId + metrics_enhanced): it invokes `_get_event_stats(discover, ...)` with an errors-only query while the outer `dataset` is metrics_(enhanced_)performance.

raw_findings.body: The top N groups are ranked by raw (downsampled) event counts while the returned series values are upsampled sums of sample_weight, so groups with high sample rates can be selected as "top" even though their upsampled counts are lower than excluded groups, and the displayed counts do not match the ranking basis.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent top-N membership and ordering versus the upsampled values shown in the chart.
raw_findings.impact: The top N groups are ranked by raw (downsampled) event counts while the returned series values are upsampled sums of sample_weight, so groups with high sample rates can be selected as "top" even though their upsampled counts are lower than excluded groups, and the displayed counts do not match the ranking basis.
raw_findings.root_cause: Only `timeseries_columns`/`y_axes` were switched to `final_columns`; the companion selection/orderby columns for top-events queries were left untransformed.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: When upsampling is enabled, also transform the field list and orderby columns (e.g., apply transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling to `self.get_field_list(...)` and map `count()` orderbys) so selection and series use the same aggregate.
raw_findings.title: Top-events path transforms timeseries columns but not selected_columns/orderby, making top-N ranking inconsistent with upsampled series
raw_findings.trigger: A topEvents query with `yAxis=count()` and `orderby=-count()` against allowlisted projects; the top-N selection query built from `selected_columns=self.get_field_list(...)` and `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` still uses raw `count()`.

raw_findings.body: Queries return stale upsampling decisions for up to 60 seconds: newly de-allowlisted projects keep returning inflated upsampled counts and newly allowlisted projects return raw counts. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called anywhere, so the documented invalidation path does not exist; additionally `cache.get`/`cache.set` add a remote cache round-trip per query whereas `options.get` is already locally cached, so the "performance optimization" can be a net loss.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Stale/incorrect count semantics for up to 60s after allowlist changes, plus dead public API (`invalidate_upsampling_cache`).
raw_findings.impact: Queries return stale upsampling decisions for up to 60 seconds: newly de-allowlisted projects keep returning inflated upsampled counts and newly allowlisted projects return raw counts. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called anywhere, so the documented invalidation path does not exist; additionally `cache.get`/`cache.set` add a remote cache round-trip per query whereas `options.get` is already locally cached, so the "performance optimization" can be a net loss.
raw_findings.root_cause: A TTL cache was introduced around option-derived eligibility without any invalidation caller and keyed by a truncatable `hash()` value.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Drop the cache layer and call `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` directly (options lookups are already cheap), or wire `invalidate_upsampling_cache` into the option-change path and use an explicit sorted-id string instead of `hash(tuple(...))` in the key to avoid collisions.
raw_findings.title: 60s eligibility cache is never invalidated (`invalidate_upsampling_cache` has no callers) and adds a remote cache round-trip per query
raw_findings.trigger: The `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes (project added/removed) while a cached eligibility entry exists for that org/project-id combination.

raw_findings.body: Misleading documentation: the stated guarantee ("always have the latest configuration state") is false at the API boundary actually used by the endpoint, inviting incorrect assumptions during debugging of stale-count reports.
raw_findings.evidence: NOTE: This function reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time,
raw_findings.failure_mode: Reviewers/maintainers rely on stale documentation that contradicts runtime behavior.
raw_findings.impact: Misleading documentation: the stated guarantee ("always have the latest configuration state") is false at the API boundary actually used by the endpoint, inviting incorrect assumptions during debugging of stale-count reports.
raw_findings.root_cause: Docstring written for uncached behavior was not reconciled with the caching added in the caller in the same patch.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the docstring to state that results are cached for 60 seconds by the public entry point, or remove the claim once the cache is removed.
raw_findings.title: Docstring claims allowlist is read fresh each call, contradicted by the new 60s cache in the caller
raw_findings.trigger: A developer reads `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` docs and assumes configuration changes take effect immediately, while `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` serves cached results for 60 seconds.

raw_findings.body: Frontend/meta consumers that format based on result type may render the upsampled count differently (e.g., with decimal formatting) than the plain `count()` it substitutes, even though the SnQL wraps the sum in `toInt64`.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent meta/formatting between upsampled and non-upsampled count columns.
raw_findings.impact: Frontend/meta consumers that format based on result type may render the upsampled count differently (e.g., with decimal formatting) than the plain `count()` it substitutes, even though the SnQL wraps the sum in `toInt64`.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new function definition copied a "number" result type from non-count aggregates instead of matching count()'s integer type.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Set `default_result_type="integer"` to match `count()` semantics and the `toInt64` wrapper.
raw_findings.title: `upsampled_count` declares default_result_type "number" despite returning an integer count
raw_findings.trigger: A query resolves `upsampled_count()`; result meta reports type "number" instead of "integer" like the `count()` aggregate it replaces.

raw_findings.body: The riskiest new logic (60s caching, cache-key hashing, combination of cached eligibility with `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) ships without any direct test, so regressions such as stale or colliding cache entries would go undetected.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Untested caching path can silently regress query-count correctness.
raw_findings.impact: The riskiest new logic (60s caching, cache-key hashing, combination of cached eligibility with `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) ships without any direct test, so regressions such as stale or colliding cache entries would go undetected.
raw_findings.root_cause: Tests were written only against the pre-existing private helper functions and omit the newly introduced cached public API.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add tests for `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` covering cache miss, cache hit returning the cached eligibility, and behavior after `invalidate_upsampling_cache`.
raw_findings.title: No unit test covers the public cached entry point `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`
raw_findings.trigger: Running the new unit test module: only private helpers are imported and exercised; the cache hit/miss/TTL logic and cache-key construction in the public function are never executed under test.

raw_findings.body: Production ingest (`_derive_client_error_sampling_rate` in event_manager) only sets `sample_rate` for allowlisted projects and rejects rates outside 0<rate<=1, but the factory sets it unconditionally, so test fixtures can carry sample_weight state impossible in production, masking bugs and making upsampling tests pass under unrealistic conditions; the broad `except Exception: pass` also hides malformed test data silently.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test fixtures diverge from production ingest semantics, reducing the fidelity of upsampling tests.
raw_findings.impact: Production ingest (`_derive_client_error_sampling_rate` in event_manager) only sets `sample_rate` for allowlisted projects and rejects rates outside 0<rate<=1, but the factory sets it unconditionally, so test fixtures can carry sample_weight state impossible in production, masking bugs and making upsampling tests pass under unrealistic conditions; the broad `except Exception: pass` also hides malformed test data silently.
raw_findings.root_cause: The test-factory helper reimplements ingest sample-rate derivation without its allowlist and range guards.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the ingest validation: only set `sample_rate` when `isinstance(client_sample_rate, (int, float))` and `0 < client_sample_rate <= 1`, and avoid the bare `except Exception`.
raw_findings.title: Factory sets sample_rate without the allowlist check and 0<rate<=1 range validation that real ingest applies
raw_findings.trigger: A test stores an event with `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` outside (0, 1] (e.g., 2.0 or -1) or for a project not in the allowlist.

validated_findings.body: The top N groups are ranked by raw (downsampled) event counts while the returned series values are upsampled sums of sample_weight, so groups with high sample rates can be selected as "top" even though their upsampled counts are lower than excluded groups, and the displayed counts do not match the ranking basis.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent top-N membership and ordering versus the upsampled values shown in the chart.
validated_findings.impact: The top N groups are ranked by raw (downsampled) event counts while the returned series values are upsampled sums of sample_weight, so groups with high sample rates can be selected as "top" even though their upsampled counts are lower than excluded groups, and the displayed counts do not match the ranking basis.
validated_findings.root_cause: Only `timeseries_columns`/`y_axes` were switched to `final_columns`; the companion selection/orderby columns for top-events queries were left untransformed.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: When upsampling is enabled, also transform the field list and orderby columns (e.g., apply transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling to `self.get_field_list(...)` and map `count()` orderbys) so selection and series use the same aggregate.
validated_findings.title: Top-events path transforms timeseries columns but not selected_columns/orderby, making top-N ranking inconsistent with upsampled series
validated_findings.trigger: A topEvents query with `yAxis=count()` and `orderby=-count()` against allowlisted projects; the top-N selection query built from `selected_columns=self.get_field_list(...)` and `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` still uses raw `count()`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 254 shows `timeseries_columns=final_columns` is transformed, but lines 255 and 259 show `selected_columns=self.get_field_list(...)` and `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` remain untransformed. For top-events queries with count() ordering, selection uses raw count() while series uses upsampled_count(), causing ranking/display inconsistency.

validated_findings.body: Queries return stale upsampling decisions for up to 60 seconds: newly de-allowlisted projects keep returning inflated upsampled counts and newly allowlisted projects return raw counts. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called anywhere, so the documented invalidation path does not exist; additionally `cache.get`/`cache.set` add a remote cache round-trip per query whereas `options.get` is already locally cached, so the "performance optimization" can be a net loss.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Stale/incorrect count semantics for up to 60s after allowlist changes, plus dead public API (`invalidate_upsampling_cache`).
validated_findings.impact: Queries return stale upsampling decisions for up to 60 seconds: newly de-allowlisted projects keep returning inflated upsampled counts and newly allowlisted projects return raw counts. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called anywhere, so the documented invalidation path does not exist; additionally `cache.get`/`cache.set` add a remote cache round-trip per query whereas `options.get` is already locally cached, so the "performance optimization" can be a net loss.
validated_findings.root_cause: A TTL cache was introduced around option-derived eligibility without any invalidation caller and keyed by a truncatable `hash()` value.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Drop the cache layer and call `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` directly (options lookups are already cheap), or wire `invalidate_upsampling_cache` into the option-change path and use an explicit sorted-id string instead of `hash(tuple(...))` in the key to avoid collisions.
validated_findings.title: 60s eligibility cache is never invalidated (`invalidate_upsampling_cache` has no callers) and adds a remote cache round-trip per query
validated_findings.trigger: The `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes (project added/removed) while a cached eligibility entry exists for that org/project-id combination.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 38 shows `cache.set(cache_key, is_eligible, 60)` with 60s TTL. Line 67 shows `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but literal search confirms no callers exist. The cache introduces staleness without invalidation mechanism, and `hash(tuple(...))` can collide across different project sets.

validated_findings.body: Misleading documentation: the stated guarantee ("always have the latest configuration state") is false at the API boundary actually used by the endpoint, inviting incorrect assumptions during debugging of stale-count reports.
validated_findings.evidence: NOTE: This function reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time,
validated_findings.failure_mode: Reviewers/maintainers rely on stale documentation that contradicts runtime behavior.
validated_findings.impact: Misleading documentation: the stated guarantee ("always have the latest configuration state") is false at the API boundary actually used by the endpoint, inviting incorrect assumptions during debugging of stale-count reports.
validated_findings.root_cause: Docstring written for uncached behavior was not reconciled with the caching added in the caller in the same patch.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Update the docstring to state that results are cached for 60 seconds by the public entry point, or remove the claim once the cache is removed.
validated_findings.title: Docstring claims allowlist is read fresh each call, contradicted by the new 60s cache in the caller
validated_findings.trigger: A developer reads `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` docs and assumes configuration changes take effect immediately, while `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` serves cached results for 60 seconds.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 50-53 show docstring claiming 'reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time' and 'always have the latest configuration state', but the public entry point at lines 30-38 caches for 60 seconds. The documentation contradicts actual behavior introduced by the same patch.

validated_findings.body: Frontend/meta consumers that format based on result type may render the upsampled count differently (e.g., with decimal formatting) than the plain `count()` it substitutes, even though the SnQL wraps the sum in `toInt64`.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent meta/formatting between upsampled and non-upsampled count columns.
validated_findings.impact: Frontend/meta consumers that format based on result type may render the upsampled count differently (e.g., with decimal formatting) than the plain `count()` it substitutes, even though the SnQL wraps the sum in `toInt64`.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new function definition copied a "number" result type from non-count aggregates instead of matching count()'s integer type.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Set `default_result_type="integer"` to match `count()` semantics and the `toInt64` wrapper.
validated_findings.title: `upsampled_count` declares default_result_type "number" despite returning an integer count
validated_findings.trigger: A query resolves `upsampled_count()`; result meta reports type "number" instead of "integer" like the `count()` aggregate it replaces.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 1051 shows `default_result_type="number"` for `upsampled_count`, while line 1038 shows `count()` uses `default_result_type="integer"`. The SnQL wraps in `toInt64` but meta reports 'number', potentially causing formatting inconsistency with the count() it replaces.

validated_findings.body: The riskiest new logic (60s caching, cache-key hashing, combination of cached eligibility with `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) ships without any direct test, so regressions such as stale or colliding cache entries would go undetected.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Untested caching path can silently regress query-count correctness.
validated_findings.impact: The riskiest new logic (60s caching, cache-key hashing, combination of cached eligibility with `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) ships without any direct test, so regressions such as stale or colliding cache entries would go undetected.
validated_findings.root_cause: Tests were written only against the pre-existing private helper functions and omit the newly introduced cached public API.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add tests for `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` covering cache miss, cache hit returning the cached eligibility, and behavior after `invalidate_upsampling_cache`.
validated_findings.title: No unit test covers the public cached entry point `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`
validated_findings.trigger: Running the new unit test module: only private helpers are imported and exercised; the cache hit/miss/TTL logic and cache-key construction in the public function are never executed under test.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 7-12 show test imports only private helpers `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`. The public cached function `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` with its 60s cache logic is not imported or tested.

validated_findings.body: Production ingest (`_derive_client_error_sampling_rate` in event_manager) only sets `sample_rate` for allowlisted projects and rejects rates outside 0<rate<=1, but the factory sets it unconditionally, so test fixtures can carry sample_weight state impossible in production, masking bugs and making upsampling tests pass under unrealistic conditions; the broad `except Exception: pass` also hides malformed test data silently.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Test fixtures diverge from production ingest semantics, reducing the fidelity of upsampling tests.
validated_findings.impact: Production ingest (`_derive_client_error_sampling_rate` in event_manager) only sets `sample_rate` for allowlisted projects and rejects rates outside 0<rate<=1, but the factory sets it unconditionally, so test fixtures can carry sample_weight state impossible in production, masking bugs and making upsampling tests pass under unrealistic conditions; the broad `except Exception: pass` also hides malformed test data silently.
validated_findings.root_cause: The test-factory helper reimplements ingest sample-rate derivation without its allowlist and range guards.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the ingest validation: only set `sample_rate` when `isinstance(client_sample_rate, (int, float))` and `0 < client_sample_rate <= 1`, and avoid the bare `except Exception`.
validated_findings.title: Factory sets sample_rate without the allowlist check and 0<rate<=1 range validation that real ingest applies
validated_findings.trigger: A test stores an event with `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` outside (0, 1] (e.g., 2.0 or -1) or for a project not in the allowlist.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 353-357 show factory sets `sample_rate` unconditionally if `client_sample_rate` is truthy, with bare `except Exception: pass`. Context at event_manager.py:785-786 shows production validates `isinstance(client_sample_rate, (int, float))` and `0 < client_sample_rate <= 1`. Factory allows invalid values that production rejects.
